# dotfiles

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
Personal Arch Linux configuration for the owner's workstations and headless hosts, managed in place from a synced checkout by setup.sh and verified by bin/dotfiles-health. It links shell, Neovim, kitty, tmux, Niri, Noctalia, systemd user units, and per-host state while keeping high-churn and machine-local files out of sync.

Authority: `docs/setup.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/desktop-themes.md`
<!-- ops:identity end -->

## Setup

This is the owner's Arch Linux configuration, with headless and platform variants.
A clone supplies tracked configuration; sibling tools and private host state are
separate prerequisites. Start with [host setup](docs/setup.md) and its read-only
preflight. Run installation only from the approved main checkout. For an isolated
code worktree, follow [development](docs/development.md) instead.

## Usage

```sh
just setup-dry-run   # preview headless link-only installation
just health         # inspect host links/config without systemd queries
just health-systemd # include user timer state
just docs           # regenerate root identity regions
just check-hygiene  # source and local record checks
```

Automatic broad tests are disabled by the validated local policy; a skip is not
a pass. Use focused checks for changed behavior. See development for deliberate
full verification, portable CI and its limits.

## Layout

- `setup.sh`, `install.toml`, `install-linux.toml`, `install-graphical.toml`, `lib/` — host installation and declarative links.
- `bin/` — health, layout, theme, desktop and application commands.
- `shell/`, `nvim/`, `kitty/`, `ghostty/`, `git/`, `tmux.conf` — shell, editor, terminal and Git configuration; shell sources hold the alias/function catalogue.
- `niri/`, `noctalia/`, `prism/`, `wali/`, `systemd/` — desktop configuration, per-host theme inputs and service sources.
- `cheatsheets/` — functional command references, opened through shell helpers.
- `docs/` — current subject references; `tests/` holds verification, `scripts/` the repository's gates and maintenance scripts, and `tools/` vendored shared tooling.

Neovim's science-project Markdown integration loads `~/d/science-md.nvim` as an
external plugin checkout. Its implementation and development history belong there;
the local plugin declaration is in `nvim/lua/user/plugins/lang.lua`.

## Consumers

Workstations and headless hosts link home/config paths into this checkout and use
`bin/dotfiles-health` to inspect installed state. Whole-directory links make
configuration edits immediately live; merging a branch can require host approval.

Setup and user units connect sibling lookout, Prism, Familiar, Wali and Resource
Pressure Alert installations. Ops and hostkit own shared tooling and storage/link
primitives. Each sibling owns its own source, installation and runtime contracts.
